issues.description: The problem statement contains a contradictory signature for the milk method: Part 2 text asks for messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (including a double parameter and volume in the return string), while the UML and earlier task descriptions define messageOnMilk():String with no parameter. The provided solution implements a no-argument messageOnMilk(). This mismatch (parameter vs no-parameter) will confuse students about the required interface/method signature and what to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the inconsistency by choosing one signature and updating all artifacts. Either: (A) Change the Part 2 textual instruction to require messageOnMilk():String and specify the return string without a volume (matching the UML and solution), or (B) if volume must be included, update the UML, interface declaration (Milkable.messageOnMilk(double)), and all implementing classes (Seal, Goat) and tests to accept a double parameter and include the volume in the returned string. Prefer option A if the intended UML and solution behavior (no parameter) is correct.

issues.description: The problem statement's Part 2 text specifies a different signature for the milk action (messageOnMilk(double milkVolume)) than the UML, template usage, and solution implementation, which all use messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This creates a semantic/signature mismatch: students following the textual instruction may implement messageOnMilk(double) while the provided template Main and the reference solution expect messageOnMilk() without parameters, leading to compilation/test failures and confusion about the correct method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement with the UML and code: change the textual instruction to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and update the example return string to "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if the intent is to include a volume, update the UML, template Main usage, and all solution classes to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust all call sites accordingly.
